title: The periodic table: Classification of elements
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for IB Diploma Chemistry (status of the source: ai-reviewed-reverified-gate-verified-2026-09-30-awaiting-human-signoff). Terms and clues: S3.1#c02 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; S3.1#c23 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; S3.1#c22 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; S3.1#c24 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition. assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Group
items.clue: A vertical column of the periodic table.

items.label: Ocean acidification
items.clue: The fall in the pH of seawater as it absorbs more carbon dioxide.

items.label: Acid rain
items.clue: Has a pH below about 5.6, caused by oxides of sulfur and nitrogen.

items.label: Oxidation state
items.clue: The charge an atom would have if all its bonds were completely ionic.

questions.stem: A small piece of sodium is added to a large volume of water containing universal indicator. Which statement describes what happens?

options.text: Hydrogen and sodium oxide form, and the oxide stays as a solid
Hydrogen gas is released, so the solution turns acidic
Hydrogen and sodium hydroxide form, so the solution turns alkaline
The sodium dissolves unchanged, and the fizzing is air escaping

questions.explanation: 2Na(s) + 2H₂O(l) → 2NaOH(aq) + H₂(g). The sodium fizzes as hydrogen is released, and the hydroxide ions formed turn the indicator to an alkaline colour.

questions.stem: Sulfur dioxide released by burning fossil fuels contributes to acid rain. What is formed when sulfur dioxide itself reacts with water, before any oxidation takes place?

options.text: Sulfuric acid, which makes the solution acidic
Sulfurous acid, which makes the solution acidic
Sulfur hydroxide, which makes the solution alkaline
No new substance, so the solution remains neutral

questions.explanation: SO₂(g) + H₂O(l) → H₂SO₃(aq). Sulfur is +4 in both SO₂ and sulfurous acid, and the acid releases H⁺ ions, lowering the pH.

questions.stem: What is the oxidation state of nitrogen in the nitrite ion?
questions.explanation: Nitrite is NO₂⁻. With oxygen −2 and the sum equal to the ion's charge: x + 2(−2) = −1, so x = +3. This matches the rule that the '-ite' ion has the lower oxidation state.

questions.stem: Bromine water is added separately to aqueous potassium chloride and to aqueous potassium iodide. Which observation is expected?

options.text: A reaction occurs with the potassium chloride only
There is no reaction with either of the two solutions
A reaction occurs with both of the salt solutions
A reaction occurs with the potassium iodide only

questions.explanation: Bromine oxidizes iodide ions, which are below it in group 17: Br₂(aq) + 2I⁻(aq) → 2Br⁻(aq) + I₂(aq), and the solution darkens to brown. Bromine cannot oxidize chloride ions, because chlorine attracts electrons more strongly than bromine.

questions.stem: Which statement about ocean acidification is correct?

options.text: Dissolved CO₂ forms carbonic acid, lowering the pH, but seawater stays alkaline
Seawater has now become acidic, with a pH below 7, because of absorbed CO₂
Acid rain falling on the sea is the main cause of the fall in seawater pH
Warmer seawater dissolves more CO₂, which is the main reason the pH is falling

questions.explanation: CO₂(g) + H₂O(l) ⇌ H₂CO₃(aq), and carbonic acid releases H⁺ ions. The average surface pH has fallen from about 8.2 to about 8.1 since pre-industrial times: seawater is less alkaline, not acidic.

questions.stem: What are the oxidation states of hydrogen in sodium hydride, NaH, and of oxygen in sodium peroxide, Na₂O₂?
questions.explanation: In NaH, sodium is +1, so hydrogen is −1 (a metal hydride contains H⁻). In Na₂O₂, 2(+1) + 2x = 0, so oxygen is −1 (the peroxide ion O₂²⁻).

questions.stem: Small pieces of lithium and of potassium are added separately to cold water. How does the reaction of potassium compare with that of lithium, and why?

options.text: More vigorous, as its outer electron is further out and more shielded
Less vigorous, as its larger nuclear charge holds its outer electron more tightly
Equally vigorous, as both are group 1 metals with one outer electron
More vigorous, as its nuclear attraction is shared among more electrons

questions.stem: Which statement about aluminium oxide, Al₂O₃, is correct?

options.text: It reacts with acids only, as every metal oxide is basic
It reacts with bases only, as it is a p-block non-metal oxide
It reacts with neither acids nor bases, being neutral
It reacts with both acids and bases, since it is amphoteric

questions.explanation: Aluminium oxide is amphoteric: it reacts with acids, for example Al₂O₃(s) + 6HCl(aq) → 2AlCl₃(aq) + 3H₂O(l), and also with bases such as sodium hydroxide. In period 3 it lies between the basic oxides of sodium and magnesium and the acidic oxides of the non-metals.

questions.stem: Every atom in an uncombined element, such as O₂ or Cl₂, has an oxidation state of zero. Why?

options.text: It has no overall charge, so each of its atoms must also be zero
Oxidation states are given only to ions, and it contains none
Its atoms are all identical, so no electrons are transferred between them
Its atoms already have full outer shells by sharing, so they need no transfer

questions.explanation: An oxidation state shows the electrons transferred in forming a bond. Between identical atoms there is no difference in attraction for electrons, so no atom gains or loses electrons relative to another, and each is zero.

questions.stem: Calcium oxide is added to water containing universal indicator. Which statement describes what happens?

options.text: Calcium hydroxide forms, so the solution turns alkaline
The mixture fizzes, as hydrogen gas is released from the water
The oxide dissolves without reacting, so the solution stays neutral
An acid forms, as with every oxide, so the solution turns acidic

questions.explanation: CaO(s) + H₂O(l) → Ca(OH)₂(aq). Calcium oxide is a basic metal oxide: the oxide ion takes H⁺ from water, and the hydroxide ions formed turn the indicator to an alkaline colour. Calcium hydroxide is only slightly soluble, but enough dissolves to make the solution alkaline.

questions.stem: The first ionization energies of magnesium and aluminium are 738 kJ mol⁻¹ and 578 kJ mol⁻¹. Which explanation of the lower value for aluminium is correct?

options.text: Aluminium's electron is removed from 3p, higher in energy than magnesium's 3s
Magnesium's filled 3s sublevel has a special stability that resists ionization
Aluminium's electron is removed from a paired orbital, where repulsion aids removal
Aluminium atoms are larger than magnesium atoms, so the outer electron is further away

questions.explanation: Magnesium is [Ne] 3s² and aluminium [Ne] 3s² 3p¹. Aluminium's electron is removed from the 3p sublevel, which is higher in energy than the 3s sublevel, so less energy is needed. This drop is evidence that the third energy level is divided into sublevels.

questions.stem: Which statement describes a characteristic property of the transition elements?

options.text: Many of them and their compounds act as catalysts
Their catalysts are consumed, so they must be added in excess
All of their compounds are coloured, even those of Sc³⁺
Each shows a single oxidation state, as group 2 metals do

questions.explanation: Catalytic activity is a characteristic property: for example iron in the Haber process and manganese(IV) oxide in the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide. The catalyst is regenerated at the end of the reaction.

questions.stem: Iron has the electron configuration [Ar] 3d⁶ 4s². Which statement about the formation of the Fe³⁺ ion is correct?

options.text: Three electrons are removed from the 3d sublevel, giving [Ar] 3d³ 4s²
Both 4s electrons and then one 3d electron are removed, giving [Ar] 3d⁵
Three electrons are added to the 3d sublevel, giving [Ar] 3d⁹ 4s²
One 3d electron is removed before the 4s electrons, as 3d⁵ is specially stable

questions.explanation: Once the 3d sublevel is occupied, the 4s electrons are the higher in energy, so they are removed first (Fe²⁺ is [Ar] 3d⁶); the third electron then comes from 3d. Fe³⁺ is [Ar] 3d⁵ (23 electrons).

questions.stem: A solution of a transition element complex looks blue in white light. On the colour wheel, blue is opposite orange. Which statement explains the blue colour?

options.text: It absorbs blue light as electrons are promoted between split d orbitals
Its electrons fall back between split d orbitals, emitting blue light
It absorbs orange light as electrons are promoted between split d orbitals
It absorbs no light at all; blue is the natural colour of the metal ion itself

questions.explanation: Promotion of an electron between the split d orbitals absorbs light of the complementary colour, orange. The remaining light, which appears blue, is transmitted to the eye.

questions.stem: The first ionization energies of phosphorus and sulfur are 1012 kJ mol⁻¹ and 1000 kJ mol⁻¹. Which explanation of the lower value for sulfur is correct?

options.text: Phosphorus's half-filled 3p sublevel has a special stability that resists ionization
Sulfur's electron is removed from a sublevel of higher energy than phosphorus's
Sulfur loses an electron from a doubly occupied 3p orbital, where repulsion raises its energy
Sulfur atoms are larger than phosphorus atoms, so their outer electron is further away

questions.stem: Copper, [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹, is a d-block element. Is copper a transition element?

options.text: No, as its atom, [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹, has a full 3d sublevel
Yes, as every metal in the d-block is a transition element
Yes, as its ion Cu²⁺, [Ar] 3d⁹, has an incomplete 3d sublevel
No, as its only ion, Cu⁺, [Ar] 3d¹⁰, has a full 3d sublevel
